Filesystem capability support makes it possible to do away with (set)uid-0
based privilege and use capabilities instead.  That is
support for capabilities but without this present patch
possible to manage a system with capabilities alone and never need to obtain
privilege via (set)uid-0.
Of course
column2: conceptually isn't quite the same as currently possible since few

column1: user applications
column2: certainly not enough to run a viable system

column1: prepared to leverage capabilities to exercise privilege.  Further
applications exist that may never get upgraded in this way
will continue to want to support their setuid-0 base privilege needs.
Where pure-capability applications evolve and replace setuid-0 binaries
desirable that there be a mechanisms by which they can contain their
privilege.  In addition to leveraging the per-process bounding and inheritable
sets
column2: this should include suppressing the privilege of the uid-0 superuser

column1: from the process' tree of children.
The feature added by this patch can be leveraged to suppress the privilege
associated with (set)uid-0.  This suppression requires CAP_SETPCAP to
initiate
column2: and only immediately affects the 'current' process (it is inherited

column1: through fork()/exec()).  This reimplementation differs significantly from the
historical support for securebits which was system-wide
has ultimately withered to a dead relic in the source of the modern kernel.

This patch represents a no-op unless CONFIG_SECURITY_FILE_CAPABILITIES is
